description: Daily Erosion Project - Soil Erosion in the Midwest is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Iowa State University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences; Iowa State University Department of Agronomy; Iowa Water Center. This site estimates soil erosion and water runoff occurring on hill slopes in Iowa and surrounding states. Estimates are based on hill slope conditions (e.g. topography, crop, precipitation) identified via remote sensing tools like satellites. Soil erosion reduces soil productivity and degrades water quality. Coverage: Iowa and surrounding states (Midwest). The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – Rainfall-induced, Landslides. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
